title: Cache Configuration
description: Learn how to configure React Query cache settings for optimal performance and user experience.

data.text: React Query maintains a query cache in memory that stores the results of every unique query key. This cache has two distinct timers that control its behavior: `staleTime` governs how long data is considered fresh, while `cacheTime` controls how long unused queries stay in memory before garbage collection removes them. Understanding both is essential for building performant React Query applications.

terms.definition: The duration in milliseconds that data is considered fresh. While fresh, React Query will not refetch the data in the background.
The duration in milliseconds that unused queries remain in the cache before being garbage collected. Formerly called gcTime in React Query v4.
The in-memory store that holds all query results, metadata, and state in React Query.

data.text: React Query exposes several configuration options that control caching behavior. The most important are `cacheTime`, `staleTime`, `refetchOnWindowFocus`, and `refetchOnReconnect`. These can be set globally on the QueryClient or overridden per query.

rows: How long unused queries stay in cache before removal

data.text: Set defaults once when creating your QueryClient. All queries in your application inherit these values unless explicitly overridden. This is the recommended approach for maintaining consistent behavior across your app.

data.title: Global cache configuration with QueryClient
data.content: Set sensible defaults at the QueryClient level so all queries inherit consistent cache behavior.

data.text: Individual queries can override global defaults. This is useful when a specific endpoint returns data that rarely changes, or when a query is expensive and should be cached for longer. Per-query overrides take precedence over global settings.

data.title: Per-query configuration override
data.content: Per-query options override global defaults for fine-grained cache control.

data.title: When to Use Per-Query Overrides
data.text: Override staleTime for data that never changes (e.g., country list: staleTime: Infinity). Override cacheTime for expensive queries that users revisit frequently. Leave refetchOnWindowFocus on for dashboard data but turn it off for form-heavy pages.

cards.title: Global Defaults
cards.description: Configured once on QueryClient. Applies to all queries uniformly.

cards.title: Per-Query Overrides
cards.description: Set directly on useQuery call. Takes precedence over global.

data.title: Exercise: Configure Cache for a Dashboard
data.description: You are building a dashboard with three data sources: user profile (rarely changes), notifications (updates every 30 seconds), and a settings page (changes on explicit save). Configure staleTime and cacheTime for each query appropriately.
steps: Set staleTime: Infinity for the user profile query.
Set refetchOnWindowFocus: false for the settings form.
Set a global cacheTime of 10 minutes for all other queries.
data.expectedOutcome: Your dashboard loads cached data instantly for the profile, polls notifications every 30 seconds, and avoids disruptive refetches while the user edits settings.

items.question: What is the difference between staleTime and cacheTime?
items.answer: staleTime controls when data is considered outdated and eligible for background refetching. cacheTime controls how long unused queries stay in memory before being garbage collected. A query can be stale while still in cache, and it can be fresh but get garbage collected if no component is using it.

items.question: What happens if I set staleTime to Infinity?
items.answer: Data is never considered stale. React Query will never background refetch it, making it behave like a client-side cache. This is ideal for static reference data like country lists or configuration values.

items.question: Can I change cacheTime after creating the QueryClient?
items.answer: You can set defaults on the QueryClient, but individual query cache times are controlled per query. To change defaults globally after creation, update queryClient.defaultOptions.queries.cacheTime.

data.title: Cache Configuration Key Points
points: staleTime controls freshness; cacheTime controls retention in memory.
Global defaults are set on QueryClient and inherited by all queries.
Per-query overrides allow fine-grained control per data type.
Balance memory usage with user experience needs.
data.takeaway: Proper cache configuration is the foundation of a performant React Query application.
